description: Demolition and rebuilding of the existing retaining wall and staircases to the Trent Park Mansion House Terrace.
reference_no_of_permission_being_relied_:
On 2 October 2017 and 5 October 2017 respectively, Berkeley Homes secured planning permission (ref. 16/04324/FUL, as amended under application ref. 19/02568/VAR) and listed building consent (ref. 16/04375/LBD) for the phased redevelopment of the former Middlesex University Campus, Trent Park for a mixed use, residential-led development. This included alterations to the Mansion House, and repair of the Terrace.

Please refer to the cover letter for further details.
decision_conditions: Prior to the commencement of works, no demolition other than the removal of stone paving and concrete panels to a maximum depth of 150mm shall take place until a written scheme of historic building investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For buildings that are included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, which shall include the statement of significance and researchobjectives, and:A. The programme and methodology of historic building investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed worksB. The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material. Reason: To ensure that the Grade II Listed buildings are conserved and enhanced in accordance with policies CP31 of the Core Strategy and DMD 44 of Enfield's Development Management Document

Prior to the commencement of works to the following statues a full method statement and detailed schedule for their conservation, repair and reinstatement shall be submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.i) 'Statue on north west end of terrace at Trent Park House' Grade II Listed Building HE Ref.1240982ii) 'Pair of sphinxes flanking steps on east side of terrace at Trent Park House' Grade II Listed Building HE Ref. 1079461The statues shall be reinstated in their historic location prior to first use of the terrace. Works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained as such.Reason: To ensure that the Grade II Listed buildings are conserved and enhanced in accordance with policies CP31 of the Core Strategy and DMD 44 of Enfield's Development Management Document

Prior to the reinstatement of urns, a method statement for their repair and reinstatement shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Notwithstanding drawing '0406 P (20) 3000', the missing urns shall be reinstated in their historic location prior to first use of the terrace. This method statement shall include the:o	Location of urnso	Method of fixingo	Method of repair to existing urnso	Details of new urns (in the event that all of the original urns cannot be located or individual urns are considered beyond repair).Works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained as such.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and safeguard the character and appearance of the Grade II listed buildings and structures.

Prior to the reconstruction work, additional drawings that show details of i)	the two under crofts (including exterior carpentry) by section and elevation at scales of between 1:50 and 1:1 as appropriateii)	the junctions between the historic terrace and West Wing terrace (including hard surfacing, walling and parapet) by section and elevation at scales of between 1:50 and 1:1 as appropriateiii)	Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the north facing brickwork of 'Bay 18' shall be finished to match the adjoining bays.shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and shall be permanently maintained as such.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and safeguard the character and appearance of the Grade II listed buildings and structures.

Notwithstanding drawing '1441/MW/MB/250 Rev A', no hedge shall be planted along the perimeter of the terrace parapet.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and safeguard the character and appearance of the Grade II listed buildings and structures.

The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of Section 18(1)(a) of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservations Areas) Act 1990 (as amended).

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans: 1441/MW/MB/250 Rev AStructural supporting documents, ref: SB/23286~02Demolition plan, ref: 0406P(18) 1000, 0406P(18) 3000Location plan: 0406P(10) 1000Existing: 0406P(15) 3000 Proposed: 0406P(20) 3000, 0406P(20) 1000Blockwork/ brickwork installation to terrace heritage walls Method Statement, ref: 03, dated 16/09/25Conservation report, dated July 2025Dismantling the terrace wall, installing infrastructure and finishes Method Statement, ref: BL-F-05aRisk Assessment & Method Statement, dated 01.09.25Terrace Wall Methodology for Stone Identification, Removal, Inventory &ReinstallationReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to the occupation, samples of the materials to be used on the external finishes (including stone and herringbone brick paving as well as facing brick, stone and mortar) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and permanently maintained as such.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and safeguard the character and appearance of the Grade II listed buildings and structures.

Prior to the commencement of works, no demolition or development other than the removal of stone paving and concrete panels to a maximum depth of 150mm shall take place until a written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, which shall include the statement of significance and researchobjectives, andA. The programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed worksB. Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefitsC. The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material.Reason: To ensure that the Grade II Listed buildings are conserved and enhanced in accordance with policies CP31 of the Core Strategy and DMD 44 of Enfield's Development Management Document
